study.title: Modulation of temporal and occipital cortex by acupuncture in non-menstrual MWoA patients: a rest BOLD fMRI study
study.study_design: Prospective clinical trial with pre-post acupuncture design and healthy control comparison group; resting-state fMRI at two timepoints in patients, one timepoint in controls
study.population: Young women (aged 18-35) with non-menstrual migraine without aura (MWoA) and age/gender/education/handedness-matched healthy controls
study.inclusion_criteria: Migraine patients: (1) right-handed, female patients aged between 18 and 35 years; (2) patients had the diagnosis of MwoA based on the International Classification of Headache Diseases III (ICHD-III) criteria; (3) patients did not receive any preventive medicine or acupuncture treatment for headache within the past 3 months; (4) the duration of migraine should be at least 6 months; (5) patients who had undergone headache episode at least once a month for the past 3 months and were not in the menstrual period when fMRI were performed; (6) patients who had signed the informed consent form. Healthy controls: right-handed female individuals who aged between 18 and 35 years and not in their menstruating period when undergoing fMRI scan were included.
study.exclusion_criteria: Migraine patients: (1) patients with alcohol or drug abuse; (2) patients with mental, neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory or renal disease, (3) patients with a history of head trauma of any other type of headache or loss of consciousness; (4) patients with contraindications to MRI such as claustrophobia; (5) patients with contraindications to acupuncture such as bleeding disorders. Healthy controls: subjects with any type of primary or secondary headache, history of a clinically significant disorder, pregnancy or breast-feeding, contraindications to MRI, severe head deformity, or intracranial lesions were excluded.

interventions.procedure_label_exact: acupuncture (electroacupuncture) at Baihui (DU20), Shuaigu (GB8), Xuanlu (GB5), and Touwei (ST8)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: DU20 and GB8 are the main points; GB5 and ST8 is the matching point
interventions.laterality_exact: Electric stimulation was applied at DU20 and GB8 on the affected side
interventions.needle_type_exact: Disposable stainless steel acupuncture needles (Huatuo brand); Sterile single-use acupuncture needle
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.35×40 mm (Huatuo brand); 25–40 mm length, 0.25 mm diameter (sterile single-use)
interventions.penetration_exact: inserted with the purpose to achieve the Deqi sensation
interventions.manipulation_exact: Sterile single-use acupuncture needle with a length of 25–40 mm and a diameter of 0.25 mm were inserted with the purpose to achieve the Deqi sensation. Electric stimulation was applied at DU20 and GB8 on the affected side. The anode and cathode of each pair of electroacupuncture were respectively connected with the needle handle on the same side of the acupoint.
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; inserted with the purpose to achieve the Deqi sensation
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: 0.1 to 1.0 mA until the patient felt comfortable
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: All acupuncture procedures were performed by the same acupuncturist with over 3 years of experience.
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: All patients agreed not to take any regular medications for migraine for the duration of the study.
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Acupoints were located according to the national standards for acupoint location (GB 12346-90); selected according to the principle of main points+syndrome differentiation

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 3.0-Tesla scanner (uMR790 platform, United Imaging Medical Systems, Shanghai, China) with a 32-channel head coil
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: (1) 3D-T1WI sequence structural imaging was performed with a T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient echo (TR=7.2 ms, TE=3.1 ms, thickness=1 mm, flip angle=10°, FOV=256 mm × 256 mm, 192 slices). (2) Functional images were acquired with a single-shot gradient recalled echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence (TR=2000 ms, TE=30 ms, thickness=3.5 mm, flip angle=90°, FOV=224 mm × 224 mm, 33 slices, matrix=64×64).
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 8 min, with a total of 240 time points
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: RESTplus (Resting-State fMRI Data Analysis Toolkit V1.8); MATLAB program (mathworks.com); SPSS 20.0
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) standard template space
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm full width at half-maximum (this step should be after the calculation of DC but before ALFF); DC smoothed spatially with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm full width at half-maximum (FWHM)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: A sponge-built head holder was used to prevent head movements. The first 10 volumes of each scan were removed to avoid instability due to T1-related relaxation effect. Realigning: the data at all time points were spatially aligned with the data collected at the first time point to obtain the head motion parameters of the subject in the scanning time series.
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: band-pass filtering range was set at 0.01–0.08 Hz to physiological level with high frequency noise
statistical_thresholds_exact: Between-group (Group 1 vs Group 2): independent samples t-test with FDR correction (voxel-level correction, P<0.001, Voxels>60)
Within-group pre vs post acupuncture: paired T test with FDR correction (voxel-level correction, P<0.001, Voxels>20)
Correlation analyses: bivariate Pearson correlation analysis, P<0.05 considered statistically significant

extraction_notes.note: In Table 2, the DC row 'Fusiform_R' has coordinates X=-30, Y=-40, Z=-25. A negative X value conventionally places this in the left hemisphere, yet the region is labeled 'Fusiform_R' (Right). Similarly, 'Fusiform_L' has coordinates X=30, Y=-6, Z=-45, which a positive X value would conventionally place in the right hemisphere. These appear to be labeling inconsistencies in the original table. Coordinates were transcribed exactly as reported.

Disease duration is reported as '1.20±8.19 (1–10)' in Table 1, but the table footnote states 'The disease duration of the migraine patients ranged from 1 year to 24 years.' The range in the table cell (1-10) is inconsistent with the footnote range (1-24 years). Transcribed as reported in table cell.

The abstract reports the MIDAS-ALFF correlation as r=0.827 with P<0.01, while the results text states P=0.0036. Both values were extracted. The r=0.343 correlation with P=0.015 is for SF-MPQ-ALFF. The abstract lists 'r=0.827, r=0.343; P<0.01, P=0.015' together, which could be confusing. Extracted separately for each correlation.
No sham acupuncture or placebo control arm was included. The study has only a verum acupuncture group and a healthy control group. Any placebo or sham acupuncture comparison is absent.
Expectancy, blinding success, credibility, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported in the paper.
Adverse events were not reported anywhere in the paper.

Deqi was intended but no formal quantitative deqi measurement tool (e.g., MASS, MGQ) or numerical deqi scores were reported. The paper only states needles were inserted 'with the purpose to achieve the Deqi sensation.'

In Table 3 (pre vs post acupuncture, ALFF and DC), the third region is labeled 'Temporal_Pole_Mid_R' in the ALFF section (coordinates 44, 15, -32) and also 'Temporal_Pole_Mid_R' in the DC section (coordinates 42, 16, -33). The abstract and main results text refer to this as 'right middle temporal gyrus.' These may be the same region referred to differently. Extracted exactly as labeled in the respective table rows.

The paper does not explicitly state whether the coordinate space is MNI or Talairach. However, given that MNI standard template space is used for normalization (explicitly stated in methods), MNI is the reported coordinate space.

No correlations between MIDAS/SF-MPQ change rates and neuroimaging metrics are reported as significant. The paper mentions these change rate variables were included in correlation analyses (MIDAS change, SF-MPQ change) but only reports significant results for baseline scores vs ALFF/DC.

The abstract text states 'Brain activities increased in the left fusiform gyrus and right angular gyrus' — however, Table 2 shows that the left fusiform gyrus is where Group2 > Group1 (i.e., Group1 shows LOWER ALFF than Group2 in ALFF section, but in the abstract it says 'increased'). This is confusing. The abstract may have intended to describe the ALFF findings as Group1 increased in left fusiform gyrus vs Group2 (consistent with the ALFF table where Group2>Group1 labels the left fusiform row). This appears to mean Group1 had higher ALFF in left fusiform than Group2. The T value is positive (5.85), consistent with Group1 > Group2 for this cluster. The contrast direction for the left fusiform was extracted as 'Group1 increased relative to Group2' based on the positive T value.

The abstract states ALFF values in 'right angular gyrus' were decreased in Group1. However, Table 2 lists Angular_R under 'Group2 < Group1' section (negative T = -4.69), meaning Group2 has lower values than Group1, i.e., Group1 has HIGHER ALFF in Angular_R. But the abstract says activities 'decreased' in the right angular gyrus. There appears to be an inconsistency between the abstract description and the table labeling. The table values (Group2 < Group1 in ALFF, negative T) have been extracted as written. This may reflect a labeling convention issue in the paper.
Recruitment period is stated as September 2021 to January 2022 at Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
